# isoniche

**isoniche** estimates the habitat niche breadth of species from counts
in several habitats, corrected for abundance.

Classic indices of niche breadth (Levins’ B, 1 - Gini or Shannon
diversity of habitat use) make rare species look like specialists: a
rare species keeps its few individuals in its preferred habitat, while
the same species, when abundant, spills into other habitats. isoniche
uses *isodars*, the relationships between a species’ densities in pairs
of habitats, to predict where individuals settle at any total abundance.
For each species it reports:

- **density-independent niche breadth**: how widely the species uses
  habitats when rare;
- **density-dependent niche breadth**: how widely it uses them when
  abundant;
- the **niche breadth curve** between the two, with bootstrap confidence
  intervals and diagnostics that say when an estimate can be trusted.

The values can be compared among species that differ in abundance.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("itai811/isoniche")
```

## What you need

Counts of each species in two or more habitats at many replicates
(sites, or repeated surveys), ideally 10 or more, most of them sampling
every habitat. Data go in long format, one row per species x site x
habitat; a community matrix (samples x species) can be converted with
[`community_to_long()`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/community_to_long.md).

## Example

Reef fishes counted in three habitats at 13 sites around Moorea:

``` r

library(isoniche)
head(moorea_fish)

# 1. how well was each species sampled in each habitat?
cov <- check_coverage(moorea_fish, species = "species", site = "site",
                      habitat = "habitat", abundance = "abundance")

# 2. niche breadth of every species, with bootstrap confidence intervals
fish <- moorea_fish[moorea_fish$species %in% c("Chaetodon ornatissimus",
  "Forcipiger longirostris", "Scarus schlegeli", "Zebrasoma scopas"), ]
nb <- niche_breadth(fish, species = "species", site = "site",
                    habitat = "habitat", abundance = "abundance",
                    n_boot = 199, seed = 1)
nb[c("species", "nb_di", "nb_di_lower", "nb_di_upper", "nb_dd")]

# 3. which estimates can be trusted, and what to do about the others
summary(nb)

# 4. niche breadth against abundance
plot(iai_curve(nb, n_boot = 99, seed = 1))
```

## Learn more

Documentation website: <https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/>

- [`vignette("isoniche")`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/articles/isoniche.md):
  get started, a complete analysis;
- [`vignette("data-preparation")`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/articles/data-preparation.md):
  data formats, sampling effort, choosing habitats, absent habitats,
  grouping sites;
- [`vignette("diagnostics")`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/articles/diagnostics.md):
  when to trust an estimate;
- [`vignette("method")`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/articles/method.md):
  how the method works.

## Citation

Granot, I., Dubiner, S. & Belmaker, J. Why abundance-based indices of
niche breadth are biased, and what can be done to improve them. *Ecology
Letters* (in revision). Itai Granot and Shahar Dubiner contributed
equally.

See `citation("isoniche")`.

## Version 1.1.0

Version 1.1.0 rewrites the core of the package, adds the functions above
and fixes several bugs of 1.0.0 (on CRAN); results can differ from
1.0.0. See [NEWS.md](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/NEWS.md).

# Package index

## Analyse your data

Estimate niche breadth for one or many species, from long-format data.

- [`niche_breadth()`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/niche_breadth.md)
  : Density-independent and density-dependent niche breadth
- [`summary(`*`<niche_breadth>`*`)`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/summary.niche_breadth.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.niche_breadth>`*`)`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/summary.niche_breadth.md)
  : Summarise niche breadth results and their diagnostics
- [`iai_curve()`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/iai_curve.md)
  : Niche breadth as a function of total abundance
- [`plot(`*`<iai_curve>`*`)`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/plot.iai_curve.md)
  : Plot niche breadth curves

## Prepare your data

- [`community_to_long()`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/community_to_long.md)
  : Convert a community matrix to long format
- [`check_coverage()`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/check_coverage.md)
  : Sampling coverage of each species and habitat
- [`group_sites()`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/group_sites.md)
  : Group nearby sites into sampling units
- [`radius_sensitivity()`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/radius_sensitivity.md)
  : Sensitivity of niche breadth to the grouping radius

## Isodars and lower-level tools

Fit isodars and compute niche breadth for one species.

- [`fit_isodars()`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/fit_isodars.md)
  : Fit isodars
- [`iai()`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/iai.md) :
  Isodar-adjusted inequality (IAI)
- [`isoderr()`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/isoderr.md)
  : Bootstrap uncertainty of the isodar-adjusted inequality
- [`pairwise_niche()`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/pairwise_niche.md)
  : Niche breadth indices from pairwise isodar parameters

## Data and simulation

- [`moorea_fish`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/moorea_fish.md)
  : Reef fishes of Moorea in three habitats
- [`simulate_isodars()`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/simulate_isodars.md)
  : Simulate abundances in habitats linked by isodars

## Package

- [`isoniche`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/isoniche-package.md)
  [`isoniche-package`](https://itai811.github.io/isoniche/reference/isoniche-package.md)
  : isoniche: abundance-independent habitat niche breadth
